messages:
elaine: follow-up from arch sync - I want to float a page-affinity driven eviction scheduler for tiny async-offloads. Trying to reduce cross-page scattering and make compaction cheaper without introducing big runtime state.

gustav: tl;dr?

elaine: idea: instead of purely LRU/timestamp evict ordering, we bias eviction candidates by a page-affinity score. When picking victims, prefer keys that free up contiguous slots on the same GPU/host page to improve subsequent coalescing. Score = locality_bonus - age_penalty.

nora: interesting. How do we compute locality without scanning a lot of metadata? We already track per-allocation page_id and slab index but don’t want expensive joins.

elaine: keep it cheap: at allocation time we tag small items with page_id and maintain per-page counters: live_count and candidate_weight. Evictor uses per-page precomputed weight to prefer pages with many reclaimable tiny slots. No deep scans.

gustav: race conditions when allocations move between pages due to compaction or device migration? page_id must be updated atomically.

elaine: yes, when we migrate an object we update its page_id and decrement/increment counters under per-page locks. For async device migration we batch counter updates to amortize cost. We'll also expose a stale counter tolerance window to avoid flipping choices too often.

nora: what's the interaction with our existing token/lease systems? If a hot key has a lease we shouldn't evict it even if page scoring favors it.

elaine: policy: leases win. Page-affinity scoring only considered among non-leased or soft-expired items. We also add tenant-weight factors so one tenant can't dominate just because they pack keys into pages.

gustav: tenant fairness is important. Add per-tenant page quotas and a decay factor that reduces score for tenants with heavy recent wins.

pager-bot: perf note: small prototype run "page_affinity_alpha" => fragmentation -7%, compaction_cycles -12%, overall evict throughput unchanged, p95 eviction latency +1.8ms.

nora: +1 but we need to ensure worst-case tails. If an attacker crafts allocations to concentrate on a few pages, they could force eviction churn on those pages.

elaine: mitigation: detect hot-page churn and lower affinity weight for pages with high churn rate; also evict across pages when churn threshold exceeded. We'll also emit alerts for suspicious page-hotness.

gustav: device interplay: when pages have device-resident ranges, freeing them may require DMA ops. How do we ensure affinity doesn't cause lots of small DMA writes?

elaine: heuristics: prefer pages with higher host-resident ratio for affinity moves. If device moves required, aggregate candidate frees into a batched device flush window. The scheduler will group per-page DMA into batched submissions to the GPU to amortize PCIe.

nora: telemetry wishlist: per-page live_count, candidate_weight, churn_rate, tenant_win_rate, evict_batch_device_size, avg_device_batch_latency.

bench-bot: queued: `bench_page_affinity --id=pa_9923 --pattern=mixed_chat_embed --runs=8` on benchpool-6.

elaine: rollout plan:
- alpha: runtime flag on dev clusters, page-affinity applies only to host-resident small objects
- beta: add device-batching heuristics and per-tenant quotas for Dedicated clusters
- GA: enable in Hosted with conservative defaults and console knobs

gustav: test plan: mixed steady-state + 20% spike tenants + malicious concentration test. Want metrics: fragmentation ratio, compaction cycles/sec, evict tail latencies, device memcpy qps.

nora: ok. please add a short design blurb in arch repo and we can coordinate infra to provision bench nodes.

elaine: will do. posting prototype code in PR later today. Thanks.

pager-bot: scheduled job: `bench_page_affinity --ref=pa_9923 --notify=#eng-runtime`
